one_line: Explains facial perception and harmony using before/after comparisons to promote a facial analysis app.

hook.what_happens: Shows a split-screen face comparison, challenging the viewer to spot the single change.
hook.why_it_works: Creates immediate curiosity and cognitive engagement through a visual puzzle.

shots.description: Close-up highlighting the nose and chin.
Second subject showing upper blepharoplasty effect.

devices.name: circular highlight overlays
devices.what_it_is: Circles focusing attention on specific facial features.

devices.name: pixel change heatmap
devices.what_it_is: A glowing overlay showing where pixels shifted between frames.

devices.name: search bar UI mockup
devices.what_it_is: A search bar showing the app name being typed.

onscreen_text.text: This is the same face twice.
One thing on it was changed.
Almost everyone points at the nose.
Your eye reads a feature against everything around it.
Almost none of them are on the nose.
One. The nose and the chin are read as one mind.
A chin that sits back leaves the nose out in front.
Bring the chin forward and the nose settles back.
Skin resting on the lashes closes the eye beneath it.
Lift the hood and the eye reads open.
Three. A face is read in thirds.
Hairline to brow. Brow to nose. Nose to chin.
Move one boundary and all three change.
None of this tells you what to do.
It tells you why one feature can't answer it.
Faces are read whole. Not feature by feature.
Push your lower jaw forward a few millimetres.
So the question was never one feature.
It's what the whole face does when it moves.
See it on your own face first.

transcript.text: This is the same face twice. One thing on it was changed.
Almost everyone points at the nose. The nose isn't what changed. The chin is.
Your eye reads a feature against everything around it.
This is every pixel that changed. Almost none of them are on the nose.
It didn't shrink. The face caught up.
One. The nose and the chin are read as one.
A chin that sits back leaves the nose out in front.
Bring the chin forward and the nose settles back. Same nose. Every time.
Two. Another face. The lid and the eye.
Skin resting on the lashes closes the eye beneath it.
Lift the hood and the eye reads open. The eye didn't grow. The cover moved.
Three. A face is read in thirds.
Hairline to brow. Brow to nose. Nose to chin.
Move one boundary and all three change.
None of this tells you what to do. It tells you why one feature can't answer it.
Faces are read whole. Not feature by feature.
Push your lower jaw forward a few millimetres. Hold it.
Now look at your nose. Watch your nose get smaller. You didn't touch your nose.
So the question was never one feature. It's what the whole face does when it moves.
A preview, not a promise. See it on your own face first.

narrative_arc: Present a visual puzzle to hook the viewer.
Reveal the counterintuitive answer (chin changed, not nose).
Prove it scientifically using pixel-change data.
Explain the principles of facial harmony (nose-chin, lid-eye, facial thirds).
Provide an interactive physical test for the viewer to experience the illusion.
Introduce the app as a tool to preview these changes.

cta.what: Search 'Refina AI' to see it on your own face first.

subjects: Unnamed Caucasian woman: Subject for chin augmentation and facial thirds analysis.
Unnamed Black woman: Subject for upper blepharoplasty analysis.
what_makes_it_work: Uses a highly engaging visual illusion to immediately hook attention.
Backs up claims with data-driven pixel analysis, building credibility.
Includes an interactive physical test that lets viewers experience the concept firsthand.

animations.name: Before-After Slider
animations.what_moves: A vertical divider line sweeps horizontally across the face.
animations.purpose: Reveals the subtle difference between the before and after states of chin augmentation.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing any two states of a visual subject, like before/after treatment or styling.

animations.name: Nose Highlight Circle
animations.what_moves: A circular outline draws itself around the nose.
animations.purpose: Directs the viewer's attention to the nose area to challenge their perception.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting a specific focal point on a product or diagram.

animations.name: Feature Callouts
animations.what_moves: Horizontal brackets and text labels fade and scale in.
animations.purpose: Labels which parts of the face were changed versus untouched.
animations.reusable_as: Labeling key components of a product or anatomical diagram.

animations.name: Pixel Change Heatmap
animations.what_moves: Before, after, and difference images swap in sequence.
animations.purpose: Shows mathematical proof of which pixels actually changed.
animations.reusable_as: Showing alignment, differences, or diagnostic overlays.

animations.name: Dimension Lines
animations.what_moves: Vertical measurement lines draw next to the nose and chin.
animations.purpose: Illustrates the proportional relationship between nose and chin height.
animations.reusable_as: Showing dimensions, heights, or scale of objects.

animations.name: Eyelid Highlight Oval
animations.what_moves: An oval outline draws around the eyes.
animations.purpose: Focuses attention on the upper eyelid hooding.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting specific regions of interest in medical or beauty ads.

animations.name: Facial Thirds Brackets
animations.what_moves: Three vertical brackets draw on the left, and a stacked bar indicator fills on the right.
animations.purpose: Divides the face into equal thirds to explain aesthetic balance.
animations.reusable_as: Showing structural divisions, grids, or layout proportions.

animations.name: Facial Mesh Overlay
animations.what_moves: A geometric wireframe mesh fades and draws over the face.
animations.purpose: Conveys a sense of high-tech analysis and facial scanning.
animations.reusable_as: Tech, AI, or scanning overlays on portraits or products.
animations.would_need_building: A custom SVG wireframe mesh that draws its paths simultaneously.

animations.name: Interactive Instructions List
animations.what_moves: Numbered list items slide in vertically one after another.
animations.purpose: Guides the user through a physical test to try on their own face.
animations.reusable_as: Step-by-step tutorials, feature lists, or instructions.

animations.name: Search Bar and Typing
animations.what_moves: A search bar pops in, text types out, and a cursor clicks.
animations.purpose: Prompts the user to search for the app name.
animations.reusable_as: Call-to-action search sequences at the end of ads.

signature_moves: TrimPath for technical measurement lines and brackets
animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements scale up with a slight spring overshoot or draw on as clean vector paths.
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements typically fade out or are replaced by hard cuts.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts between different subjects and analytical views.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The primary portrait photos remain centered and static.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Bursty and educational, with animations timed to match the voiceover explanations.

what_we_should_steal: The SliderReveal before/after comparison tool for interactive visual demonstrations.
The TrimPath measurement brackets for clean, technical-looking product breakdowns.
